findings.highlight: She can sit up on her own
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか一人で体を起こせるぐらい
findings.governingReading: Sakura has recovered only to the point where she can just barely raise herself unaided.
findings.explanation: The English reports independent sitting without the limiting “barely manages” qualification.

findings.governingReading: Given Sakura’s visible improvement, Shirou cannot make the claim that she has only days left feel real.
findings.explanation: The English drops the negation and reverses disbelief into belief.

findings.evidenceJa: えへへ、と桜にしては珍しい照れ笑い
findings.governingReading: Sakura gives an “ehehe” shy laugh unusual for her.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the audible manner and Shirou’s observation that it is rare for Sakura.

findings.governingReading: As a child Shirou blamed his pain and fever on medicine that felt unfamiliar and unknowable.
findings.explanation: The English removes the medicine’s alien, untrustworthy quality.

findings.highlight: I have to keep my feelings frozen
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を捕まえたくなる衝動を、凍らせた心で押し止める
findings.governingReading: Shirou uses his frozen heart to suppress the impulse to seize Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits the concrete impulse and the action his emotional restraint prevents.

findings.governingReading: Sakura reacts with visible, flustered bewilderment.
findings.explanation: The English turns her agitated response into quiet thought.

findings.governingReading: Sakura voices a small, modest wish.
findings.explanation: The English calls the wish trivial, adding dismissive judgment.

findings.highlight: I want to go cherry blossom viewing
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩とお花見がしたいです
findings.governingReading: Sakura specifically wants to view blossoms with Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English omits the person whose company constitutes the wish.

findings.evidenceJa: 四月にさえなれば幾らでも叶えられる願い
findings.governingReading: Once April arrives, this is an ordinary wish that could be fulfilled any number of times.
findings.explanation: The English preserves eventual possibility but loses its easy repeatability and the pathos of how modest it is.
